subject: Orchid Health — stalled completions & p99 queueing (urgent)
messages:
From: Mina Haddad <mina@redwood.com>

Cc: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 25 Aug 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Orchid: observed stalled completions & p99 queueing (urgent)

Hi Samantha —

Thanks for flagging this. I can see the support ticket and the dashboard spikes you linked. Our immediate priority is to stop customer-facing errors and reduce the long-tail p99s while we triage root cause (queueing/backpressure vs model-side timeouts).

Immediate actions I propose (we can run these in parallel):
- Engineering will enable a temporary fallback route to the quantized model variant (10% traffic first) to confirm whether the long tail is model-side.
- We will raise the concurrency cap on your dedicated pool by one slice for the next 2 hours (if you approve) to relieve queuing at the queue-processor layer.
- We'll enable prefix/KV cache warming for the busy routes and flush any stale shard partitions.

Please attach the sample request logs (one or two slow traces) and confirm whether we can run a 30-minute maintenance window to toggle the fallback. I've attached a small checklist for the data we'll need.

Attachments: orchid-request-sample.log.txt (please add 3–5 offending request IDs)

I’ve looped in Dev and Marissa for engineering and customer comms. We’ll update you within 90 minutes after actions start.

—Mina

—Samantha

Date: Fri, 25 Aug 2028 11:35:42 -0700
Subject: Re: Orchid: observed stalled completions & p99 queueing (urgent)

Quick triage notes after a first-pass on the logs Samantha sent:
- We see long-lived requests building in the request queue; many of the slow traces show identical prefix tokens and high KV-cache miss rates. That suggests the heavy tail is driven by cold KV shards + some requests degenerating into longer decode loops (rare prompts).
- There are also intermittent backend 502s coming from an internal inference worker that hit a GC spike (Java-based coordination service).

Proposed immediate engineering steps (30–90m window):
1) Activate 10% fallback route to redwood-14b-quantized (lower mem, predictable latency) — traffic will be sampled across session IDs.
2) Temporarily increase concurrency cap by +1 slice on Orchid's dedicated pool (if infra approves) for 2 hours to drain queues.
3) Enable prefix caching warming on the busiest route and pin popular KV shards to the hot cache.
4) Short-term rate limiting: apply a soft per-tenant request-funneling (max inflight per tenant = 8) to reduce long-hang requests starving queue slots.

I will open an infra ticket to check the worker GC patterns. If we see worker instability persist, we should fail traffic to a different region/variant.

I’ll prepare the rollback steps for each action.

—Dev
Dev Patel
Senior SRE, Serving Runtime
dev_patel@redwood.com

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 26 Aug 2028 08:15:00 -0700
Subject: Internal: playbook + exec note for Orchid escalation

Team — drafting a concise exec-facing update and the internal playbook. Copying the high-level bullets we should include in the customer update:
- What happened: transient request pileup causing p99 degradation and a small rise in 5xx errors; likely contributors: KV cache misses + a GC spike on a worker group.
- Immediate mitigation (in flight): 10% fallback to quantized variant; +1 dedicated slice; prefix cache warm; soft per-tenant inflight cap.
- Next 24h plan: continue trace collection; replace affected worker VMs; run a controlled replay on staging to reproduce long-tail conditions; instrument request sampling for long-hang traces.
- Metrics to watch: p50/p90/p99, inflight queues, KV miss rate, worker GC pause time.

Operational ask for execs: approve short maintenance window and the temporary capacity increase (this is billable but minimal). If approved, Mina can send the customer-facing note.

Runbook location: runbook-long-tail-drain-v1.md (internal)

I’ll prepare an SLA impact note for sales if we exceed 4% error-rate for >30m.

—Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Principal Engineer, Inference Runtime

From: Mina Haddad <mina@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Cho <samantha.cho@orchidhealth.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 26 Aug 2028 13:40:00 -0700
Subject: Orchid escalation — immediate mitigations scheduled (please confirm)

Samantha —

Thanks for the quick upload. We’ve scheduled the immediate mitigations to start at 14:10 PT (short maintenance window ~30 minutes):
- Route 10% of traffic to redwood-14b-quantized (warm path) to test whether the model variant reduces p99 without losing output quality.
- Increase dedicated pool concurrency by +1 slice for Orchid for 2 hours to allow queues to drain.
- Enable prefix caching warming and pin top 5 KV shards.
- Apply soft per-tenant inflight cap = 8 for 40 minutes (will be removed sooner if p99 stabilizes).

Please confirm you are comfortable with the maintenance window and that we have permission to temporarily change routing. We’ve attached a one-click approval pdf if you need internal sign-off: orchid-maintenance-approval.pdf

We’ll update you at T+15m and T+45m with metrics and next steps.

Best,
Mina

From: Samantha Cho <samantha.cho@orchidhealth.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina@redwood.com>
Cc: Orchid Health SRE <sre@orchidhealth.com>, Anna Li <anna.li@orchidhealth.com>
Date: Mon, 27 Aug 2028 09:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Orchid escalation — immediate mitigations scheduled (please confirm)

Mina —

Confirmed and approved. We saw the p99 drop back to ~1.1s during the 10% fallback test window and error-rate returned to baseline after the +1 slice drain. The SRE team wants the audit logs for the change and a short postmortem once you have root cause.

Please add the audit export to the ticket and we’ll coordinate a follow-up call Wednesday to review the replay results and longer-term fixes.

Thanks for the rapid support — your team moved fast.

—Samantha
